<Myth busters>

What an FDE is not

Myth 01
"It is only really for backend engineers."
Reality
SRE, QA/SDET, Data, Cloud, Security, TPM, EM, and more all have a mapped route in - we'll break each one down shortly.
Myth 02
"It is heads-down coding - no stakeholder work."
Reality
You work across Product, Solutions, Sales, and Customer Success. That is the opportunity, not a distraction from it. Now that's the opportunity.
Myth 03
"You have to work from the customer's office."
Reality
FDEs work with the customer's technology - not necessarily from their office. Most roles today are remote or hybrid.
Myth 04
"You are a one-person army, alone at the customer site."
Reality
There are levels - from Associate to Principal, IC to Lead. You work with Product, ML, Engineering, and the customer team. We'll break this down further shortly.
In reality, FDE is a structured career with clear levels, strong teamwork, and defined growth opportunities.

Why this role exists

0
Pilots Failed

MIT: enterprise GenAI pilots delivering no measurable business impact

The cause was deployment, not the models

  • ▸Models got good. Making them work inside a real enterprise did not.
  • ▸The hard part is everything around the model - security & compliance, data quality, integration, governance, change management.

The value and the hiring moved to the person who closes that gap in the field.

Who is an FDE?

Role. Engagement.

<The FDE Story>

How it all started.

The role wasn't created. It evolved to solve real-world problems.

A journey from the battlefield to the boardroom
1950s - Today
Military Origin
“Forward deployed” meant being closest to the mission - where decisions had to be made.
2008 - 2016
Palantir Era
Palantir popularised the “Forward Deployed Engineer” role by embedding engineers alongside defence, intelligence and government customers to solve mission-critical problems.
2020 - 2025
Enterprise AI Revolution
LLMs became powerful. But enterprises still struggled to deploy, integrate and scale AI in production.
2026 and Beyond
Forward Deployed AI Engineer
Engineers who build AI, deploy it, and drive customer outcomes.
It sits at the intersection of three critical worlds
Where AI, Systems, and People meet to create IMPACT
★Most tech folks have one or two. The FDE has all three - that is the whole scarcity.

<Hiring Manager - Point Of View>

Hiring an FDE is a trust decision before it's a technical decision.

Because you'll work closely with customers, hiring managers focus on three core areas.

FEAR 01 "Can they build it?"
82%
of FDE job descriptions require AI/ML

Table stakes - and the easiest of the three to prove.

FEAR 02 "Will they survive the customer?"
92%
of FDE work happens in collaboration with customers

The one most tech folks have zero evidence for.

FEAR 03 "Will it still run after they leave?"
~95%
of pilots died before production

They have been burned before - that is why the role exists.

The bar is not more years - it is evidence across all three. That is why a 4-year tech person with one deployed system beats a 12-year tech person with none.
Share requiring AI/ML, customer-facing and embedded shares: analysis of 531 active LinkedIn FDE job descriptions, Jul 2026 · pilot failure rate: MIT NANDA

<CHAPTER 04>

A structured path

Back to Raghav - the program, week by week

<The 30-second scan>

What a hiring manager actually reads

Headline - positioned as someone who ships production AI inside customer environments (not "AI enthusiast")
A hero deployment - one flagship system: scoped → built → deployed → handed over, with a number on the outcome
Outcome bullets, not tool lists
✗"Built a bot with LangChain"
✓"Deployed a multi-agent RAG assistant for a Fortune-100 bank's support org - cut handle time 35%, owned discovery to handover"
Evidence - GitHub (deployed, dense graph) + a short writeup or demo link - proof it's real, not a slide deck

Don't have an external customer? Build it for a team inside your own company instead - start to finish. It still counts as a real project on your resume.

Why you need a structured path

Tool demos→Production systemsOrchestration, safety, evaluation, cost control, deployment - not isolated LLM demos.
Using AI→Engineering judgmentWhen to use agents vs deterministic systems, and how to defend the trade-off.
Traditional engineering→FDE craftDiscovery, scoping, commercials, governance, customer handover.
Generic interview prep→This exact loopDecomposition, client simulation, AI system design, procurement-security drill.
One stack→Three stacksOpenAI + AWS primary, plus Google ADK + Vertex and Claude + Azure.
The FDE programs in India today are academic credential tracks or self-serve content. A live cohort combining all three layers doesn't exist here yet.
